text.content:
• Units, not soldiers: an army is made of units, bodies of soldiers who share a people, training, gear and type. A unit might be fifty spears or five thousand; the rules don't change.
  • Casualties: losses are counted in casualties, which stand for soldiers dead, fled, lost or too shaken to obey.
  • Commanders: each unit answers to a commander. Player characters usually command from behind the lines while their army fights the enemy's.
  • Speed: a battle is meant to run faster than an ordinary fight, and it often runs alongside one (see Heroes in battle).

• The grid: each side has a grid 5 spaces wide and 4 ranks deep. From the front, its ranks are the Vanguard, Reserve, Centre and Rear. The two grids meet at the Vanguards.
  • On the grid: infantry, archers and siege engines stand on the grid.
  • Off the grid: cavalry and flying units stand beside it and can reach anywhere.
  • Adjacent means next to, along a row or a column, never on a diagonal.
  • Size of battle: a good battle has 12 units a side or fewer. For more, add a column for every 3 units over 15.
  • Collapsing ranks: at the start of each round, an empty rank with no fortification in it disappears, and the ranks either side close up.

StatWhat it does
Attackd20 + Attack against the target's Defence. A hit deals 1 casualty, and you then roll Power
DefenceWhat enemies must reach with Attack
Powerd20 + Power against the target's Toughness. A success deals casualties equal to the unit's Damage
ToughnessWhat enemies must reach with Power
MoraleA Morale Score of 2 to 12, as for monsters. A Morale check is 2d6: roll higher than the score and the unit fails
Commandd20 + Command for manoeuvres (Follow Up, Brace, Retreat)
AttacksHow many attacks it makes with one action
DamageExtra casualties on a successful Power roll
SizeThe unit's casualty die: Size 1d6 means it starts with 6 casualties to lose. Never more than 1d12
  • Bonuses to morale: a bonus "to Morale" raises the Morale Score, as the Handbook says (12 at most). The Knight's Battle Lord works this way.

Building a unit

  • Starting point: start from its type, then apply its experience, its equipment and its people.

Base unit (regular, light equipment)

Siege engine+29+396−13
  • Infantry attack adjacent units only, never cavalry or flying.
  • Archers stand in the Centre and can attack any unit.
  • Cavalry stand off the grid and attack cavalry and exposed units.
  • Flying units stand off the grid and can attack any unit; only archers and flying units can attack them.
  • Siege engines stand in the Centre and can attack any unit. They must spend a round idle between shots, and always hit fortifications.

Equipment

Peoples

  • Each unit takes one trait from its people.
  • A unit raised by your stronghold is of your people unless an ambassador says otherwise.
PeopleTrait
HumanAdaptable: once per battle, reroll a failed Morale check
DwarfStalwart: +1 Toughness; can't be pushed or moved against its will
ElfKeen-Eyed: archers have +1 Attack; forest doesn't slow it
GnomeSpell-Wise: Advantage on rolls against battle magic
HalflingLucky: once per battle, reroll one Attack or Power roll
OrcRelentless: once per battle, when broken, it fights on until the end of its next activation, then breaks
HobgoblinWarbred: +1 Command, and Advantage on Follow Up
GoblinSwarm: Size one die smaller and Morale −1, but two goblin units muster as one
GnollRush: +1 movement when it moves towards an enemy
LizardfolkAmphibious: mud, rivers and rain don't slow it
AasimarRadiant: Advantage on Morale checks against undead and fiends, which have Disadvantage on Morale checks against it
UndeadMindless: never makes Morale checks, and can't be rallied

Monsters as units

  • When to use it: a monster is a unit only when the heroes wouldn't rather fight it themselves. A dragon is an encounter at 5th level, and a unit at 15th.
  • Stats:
    • Attack and Power are half its Level + 2.
    • Defence and Toughness are 10 + half its Level.
    • Morale is its Morale Score.
    • Damage is 1, or 2 if Huge, or 3 if Gargantuan.
    • Size is 1d6 for a pack or Large creature, 1d8 for Huge, 1d10 or 1d12 for Gargantuan.
  • Traits: add one or two traits from its block, for example Fearsome (dragons, demons, the dead): the first time a unit attacks it, that unit makes a Morale check, and on a failure its activation ends.
  • Solo rules: a monster unit never uses solo rules or villain actions. It is one unit, and it takes one activation like any other.

• From your stronghold: units raised by a keep (Chapter 1) or from your follower table (Chapter 3) cost nothing to raise. You pay their upkeep, which the stronghold's taxes cover (Chapter 5).
  • Mercenaries: a mercenary unit costs one season's upkeep to hire, then its upkeep each season.
  • Upkeep each season:
UnitUpkeep (gp a season)
Green infantry or archers450
Regular infantry or archers900
Cavalry2,400
Flying3,600
Siege engine600
  • Upkeep adjustments:
    • Seasoned and veteran units cost half again. Elite units cost double.
    • Heavy equipment costs half again.
    • A keep cuts upkeep by 10% per level.
  • Going unpaid:
    • A unit unpaid for a season has its Morale cut by 2.
    • A unit unpaid for two seasons goes home.
  • Better gear: a unit's equipment goes up one step for 50 gp × its Size die's largest number, light to medium, then double that for medium to heavy. A Miner artisan does it for free.
  • Class armies: the Barbarian's Warlord and the Cleric's Holy Campaign field one unit for every 50 troops, rounded up: regular light infantry, Size 1d6. The Knight's followers make one green infantry unit (Size 1d4) for every 40 who stay.

• How many units: a character commands 1 unit, +1 at 4th, 8th, 12th, 16th and 20th level. A Knight commands one more.
  • Enemy commanders: an enemy commander uses the same scale by its Level.
  • Every unit needs a commander at the battle. If its commander falls or flees, the unit makes a Morale check at once. After that, its sergeants keep it fighting.
  • Orders:
    • Each player character commander knows one Order from their class's list, two from 8th level and three from 16th.
    • Each Order can be given once per battle, on your side's turn, to a unit you command.
OrderClassesEffect

Before the battle

  • Choosing the ground: if both sides are looking for the fight, each leader makes a Hard Intelligence check. The winner chooses whether to attack, defend its stronghold or fight in open ground.
  • Deployment:
  • Roll side initiative, as the Handbook allows for mass battles. The loser deploys first.
  • Infantry deploy in any rank.
  • Archers and siege engines deploy in the Centre.
  • Cavalry and flying units deploy off the grid.
  • The attacker's first strike: the side that brought the battle may give each unit in its Vanguard one free activation before the first round.

Each round

  • Initiative: roll side initiative each round. The winning side takes its whole turn first.
  • Activations: on your side's turn, each commander activates each of their units, one at a time. A unit may:
    • move 1 space and act, or act and then move;
    • march (move 2 spaces);
    • or hold.
  • Actions: attack, or try a manoeuvre.
  • Movement:
    • Movement is into an empty space, never on a diagonal and never through another unit.
    • A unit that moves backwards off its own Rear rank has left the battle for good.

Who can attack whom

  • Infantry: adjacent units, but never cavalry or flying.
  • Archers and siege engines: any unit.
  • Cavalry: other cavalry, and exposed infantry, archers or siege engines.
  • Flying: any unit. Only archers and flying units can attack them.
  • Exposed: a unit is exposed if it has no unit between it and either side edge of the field, or no unit in any rank behind it.
    • A unit in the Rear rank is always exposed.
    • A unit in a fortification never is.

Attacking

  • Roll d20 + Attack against the target's Defence. On a hit, the target takes 1 casualty.
  • Then roll d20 + Power against its Toughness. On a success, it takes casualties equal to your Damage.

Advantage and Disadvantage work as in the Handbook.

Diminished and broken

  • Diminished: when a unit is down to half its Size or less, it is diminished. The first time this happens in a battle, it makes a Morale check, and on a failure it takes 1 casualty.
  • Broken: at 0 casualties left, the unit is broken and leaves the field.

Morale checks

  • When a unit checks:
    • the first time it is diminished;
    • when its commander falls or flees;
    • the first time it attacks a Fearsome unit;
    • when its fortification falls (with Disadvantage);
    • when an Order or a trait says so.
  • The result: a failed check costs 1 casualty unless the rule says otherwise.

Manoeuvres

Manoeuvres are d20 + Command.

  • Follow Up (infantry): once per round, out of turn, when an adjacent enemy breaks or leaves its space, DC 8: move into that space.
  • Brace (infantry): once per round, out of turn, when cavalry or flying units deal it a casualty in melee, DC 13: the attacker takes 1 casualty.
  • Retreat (any unit, as its action): DC 8.
    • Success: the unit leaves the battle in good order.
    • Failure: it takes 1 casualty first, then leaves if it still can.

Victory

  • Unit value: each unit is worth 1, +1 if seasoned, veteran or elite, +1 if heavy, and +1 if a monster of Level 10 or more.
  • The check: at the end of each round, total the value of each side's units still on the field. A side worth more than twice the other wins.
  • The losing side: every unit on the losing side tries to Retreat at once.

FortificationSpacesMorDefArcher PowHP
Stone wall or ditch1–2+1+2—4
Tower1+1+2+26
Town wall3–4+1+2—8
Gatehouse5+2+2+28
Keep2 × 2+2+2+210
Castle4 × 2+3+2+212
  • Who benefits: the Morale bonus goes to every one of its side's units on the field; only the highest counts. Defence and Power go to units inside it.
  • Moving in: entering a fortification space costs a whole move; leaving is free.
  • Contested: once an enemy unit is inside, no one gets its Morale bonus.
  • Damage: only siege engines and units whose traits say so can damage a fortification. A siege engine always hits for 1d4 + 2.
  • When it falls: at 0 HP the fortification falls, and every unit that was in it makes a Morale check with Disadvantage.
  • Your stronghold: a stronghold fights as its fortification (Chapter 1).

Ground

  • Forest or fog: archers have Disadvantage on Attack.
  • Mud or deep snow: moving 1 space takes a march.
  • Rain: counts as both mud and fog.
  • Open plains: cavalry have +1 Command.
  • Hills: a unit charging downhill has Advantage on its first Attack; a march uphill needs a DC 8 Command roll or it moves only 1 space.
  • Bridges and passes: the Vanguard is one space wide, and cavalry can't fight there.

• Behind the lines: player characters usually fight the enemy commanders, champions and monsters in an ordinary encounter, while the armies fight around them.
    • Run one battle round, then one encounter round, and so on.
    • When an enemy commander falls or flees, each unit they led makes a Morale check at once.
    • If the heroes are beaten, every unit they led tries to Retreat.
  • Leading a unit: a character may instead fight inside a unit.
    • The unit has Advantage on its Morale checks.
    • When the unit breaks, the character is left in an ordinary encounter with whatever broke it.
  • Champions: when two units led by commanders are adjacent, one commander may call the other out. If the other accepts, the battle waits while the two fight. The loser's unit takes 1 casualty for each round the duel lasted.
  • The Knight's Battle Lord (19th): allied units that can see the knight fight (leading a unit, or in the encounter beside them) gain the following. It works on units only, never on player characters or retainers.
    • +1 Defence and +1 Morale (12 at most).
    • They add the knight's Charisma modifier to their Power rolls.
    • 24th level: +2 Defence, +2 Morale, and twice the Charisma modifier.
    • If the knight leaves the field or falls, each of them makes a Morale check at once with its Morale cut by 4. A unit that must also check because its commander fell makes one check, not two.

• Rally: each broken unit makes a Morale check. On a success it returns with 1 casualty; on a failure it disbands.
  • Recovery: surviving units regain 1 casualty a week until they're whole.
  • Experience: a unit that survives a battle gains experience:
    • green to regular after 1 battle;
    • regular to seasoned after 1 more;
    • seasoned to veteran after 2 more;
    • veteran to elite after 4 more.
  • Afterwards: loaned and allied units go home, and any effects from the battle end.
